title: Maximum Number of Eaten Apples
summary: Given two arrays, apples and days, each of length n, where apples[i] represents the number of apples grown on the i-th day and days[i] indicates how many days those apples remain fresh, determine the maximum number of apples you can eat over n days, eating at most one apple per day.
statement: Given two arrays, apples and days, each of length n, where apples[i] represents the number of apples grown on the i-th day and days[i] indicates how many days those apples remain fresh, determine the maximum number of apples you can eat over n days, eating at most one apple per day. If no apples are grown on a day, both values are zero.
constraints: apples and days have equal length up to 20000; a zero apple count has zero shelf life.
Apples grown on day i rot at the start of day i+days[i].
Eat at most one apple per day, continuing after the growing period, to maximize the total eaten.
hints: When eating today, choose the available apple with the earliest expiration.
A min-heap stores batches by expiration day and remaining count.
Add today’s batch, remove expired/empty batches, consume one from the earliest expiration, and continue while production or inventory remains.
An exchange argument replaces any later-expiring apple eaten before an earlier one without hurting future feasibility, proving the greedy order.

tests.explanation: Always consuming the earliest-expiring available batch allows seven apples to be eaten.
Eat three early apples before day three and both later apples before day seven, totaling five.
